mainTopic: How a כתם works for women who are דיין שעתן, and when a checking cloth used during תשמיש counts as a פקידה
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier answer: the משנה follows רבי דוסא, and the ברייתא is a ruling everyone agrees with. The גמרא asks why we don't flip this, and answers that when a text can be read leniently or strictly, we read it לחומרא. Next, the גמרא infers from the ברייתא that for women who are דיין שעתן, a כתם is treated like a ראייה. It identifies this as the view of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, who also says a young girl before the age of seeing has no כתם at all. A second ברייתא seems to say he holds these women have no כתם whatsoever. The גמרא explains that he means only that it is not retroactive, and that the opposing view is רבי מאיר, who is strict about כתמים. Then the גמרא turns to checking cloths during תשמיש: שמואל rules that a cloth used before תשמיש does not count as a פקידה, because in her rush she does not check thoroughly. The גמרא defends this against the plural 'עדים' in the משנה with two different answers. It ends by starting a new question about the משנה's words 'it reduces from מעת לעת', which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא is everyone's opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier answer by saying the ברייתא is a ruling that all opinions accept.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the ברייתא follows everyone's opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer that began earlier on the דף. The משנה was explained as רבי דוסא's view, and here it says the ברייתא is a ruling everyone agrees with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that blood seen not at the woman's set time makes her impure going back twenty-four hours. On that point all opinions agree. So the משנה and ברייתא no longer clash, because each one is explained in its own way.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
Everyone's opinion; all sides agree

phrases.english: And the baraita is the opinion of everyone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the resolution started before this section: משנה = רבי דוסא, ברייתא = everyone.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different opinion
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's ruling on blood seen outside the set time is agreed by all.

steps.title: Why not explain it the other way around?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: why not make the משנה everyone's opinion and the ברייתא just one side's opinion?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us explain it the opposite way!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. It asks why we don't flip the two explanations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה carries more weight than a ברייתא. So it would seem better to say the משנה is everyone's view, and the ברייתא follows only the רבנן. The challenge is: why choose the explanation that pushes the משנה into a single opinion?

keyTerms.meaning: Let us explain or set up the source as following a certain view
The opposite; the reverse way

phrases.english: But let us explain it the opposite way!
phrases.notes: He means: make the משנה everyone's opinion, and the ברייתא only the רבנן's opinion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the way step 1 assigned the opinions.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to explain the משנה as רבי דוסא and the ברייתא as everyone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה is more authoritative, so it should be the one read as everyone's opinion.

steps.title: When in doubt, choose the strict reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that when there is a lenient reading and a strict reading, we pick the strict one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it can be explained in a way that leads to a leniency or in a way that leads to a stringency, we explain it in the way that leads to a stringency.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its first answer with a rule. If a reading could lead to a קולא or a חומרא, we go with the חומרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making the משנה everyone's view would mean all agree that blood seen at her set time is only impure from now on. That is the lenient result. The chosen reading has everyone agree that blood outside her set time is impure going back, and has the רבנן say this even at her set time. That is the strict result, so we choose it.

keyTerms.meaning: A leniency
A stringency
We explain it as; we set it up as

steps.whatToRemember: When a source can be read in a lenient way or a strict way, the גמרא here chooses the strict reading (לחומרא מוקמינן).
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the גמרא chose a reading that seems less natural at first. In matters of טומאה it takes the safer, stricter path.

phrases.english: Since there is a way to explain it
as a leniency and as a stringency —
phrases.notes: The flipped reading leads to a leniency, and the original reading leads to a stringency.

phrases.english: we explain it as a stringency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A general rule for choosing between readings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think the משנה should be everyone's opinion because it carries more weight.
steps.terutzMaskana: We keep the reading that leads to a stringency, so the ברייתא is everyone's view and the משנה is רבי דוסא's.

steps.title: Looking closely at the ברייתא's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's reason. It notes that the רבנן treat a woman with a וסת differently for a כתם than for a ראייה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: for if she sees blood not at the time of her set cycle, she makes things impure going back twenty-four hours. The reason is that she is a woman who has a set cycle, which is why the רבנן draw a difference between her stain and her seeing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new look at the ברייתא and points out its reason. This is setting up the inference the גמרא draws in Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ties the ruling to the woman having a וסת. For her, a כתם is treated like blood seen outside her set time, so it makes things impure going back. Her ראייה at the set time does not. Saying the reason depends on her having a וסת hints that a woman without a וסת might be treated differently. The גמרא will pick that up next.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman's set, predictable menstrual time
A twenty-four-hour period; impurity that reaches back that long
A blood stain found, not a flow that was felt or seen coming
Seeing an actual flow of blood
The reason

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up כתם and ראייה. A כתם is a stain she finds afterward. A ראייה is seeing the flow itself. The ברייתא's whole point is that these two can be treated differently.

phrases.english: It teaches: for if she sees
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא's reason why a woman with a set cycle who finds a stain is impure going back.

phrases.english: not at the time of her set cycle
she makes impure going back twenty-four hours.

phrases.aramaic: טַעְמָא דְּאִשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת הוּא,
phrases.english: The reason is that she is a woman who has a set cycle,
which is why the Rabbis distinguish
between her stain and her seeing,

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי: שֶׁאִם תִּרְאֶה שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת וִסְתָּהּ מְטַמְּאָה מֵעֵת לְעֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the משנה-versus-ברייתא question and opens a close reading of the ברייתא's reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a woman with a וסת, the רבנן treat her כתם as impure going back, unlike her ראייה at her set time. The reason depends on her having a וסת.

steps.title: Inference: For other women whose time is enough, a stain is like a sighting
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא's special rule for a woman with a וסת, the גמרא infers the rule for other women who are דיין שעתן: their כתם is treated like their ראייה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that other women, about whom the חכמים said 'their time is enough,' have stains that are treated like their sightings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the ברייתא. Only the woman with a וסת is treated differently, so all other דיין שעתן women have a כתם that works just like their ראייה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 showed that the רבנן split the woman with a וסת: her כתם is not treated like her ראייה. That implies the other דיין שעתן women, such as a pregnant or elderly woman, are not split. For them, a כתם is like a ראייה, so it does not make things טמא retroactively.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Their time is enough': these women become טמא only from the moment they see blood, not retroactively.
A blood stain found on a garment or body, without feeling the blood come out.
A 'sighting': actually seeing menstrual blood come out.
Other women, the rest of the women in this category.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up כתם and ראייה. A ראייה is actually seeing the flow. A כתם is just finding a stain afterward, without knowing exactly when it came.

phrases.english: This implies that other women
phrases.notes: He means women other than the woman with a וסת we just discussed, such as a pregnant or elderly woman.

phrases.english: about whom the Sages said: their time is enough
their stains are like their sightings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the implied rule for other women from the special treatment of the woman with a וסת in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For other women who are דיין שעתן, a כתם is treated like a ראייה, meaning no retroactive טומאה.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the view that a כתם is like a ראייה for דיין שעתן women.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the author of this view is. This one-word question sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference from Step 5 is a specific position, and not everyone holds it. So the גמרא wants to know which תנא it matches.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who is it?' A question asking which תנא's opinion a teaching follows.
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה.
A sage from the time of the משנה.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the author of the inference just drawn.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a כתם is like a ראייה for women who are דיין שעתן.

steps.title: It is רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, who treats their stain like their sighting
steps.stepSummary: The view belongs to רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס. He holds that most women's כתם is retroactive, but for דיין שעתן women the כתם is like their ראייה. A young girl who has not reached the age of seeing is completely excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס. As רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, quoting רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס: For all women, their stains make things טמא retroactively. But for women about whom the Sages said 'their time is enough,' their stains are like their sightings. The exception is a young girl who has not yet reached the age of seeing blood: even if her sheets are covered in blood, we are not concerned about her at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the view belongs to רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, and quotes his full ruling as a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His ruling has three levels. Regular women: a כתם is retroactive. דיין שעתן women: a כתם is like a ראייה, so it is not retroactive. A young girl who has not reached the age of seeing: her stains are ignored completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Retroactively: going back in time before the blood was found.
A young girl who has not yet reached the age of seeing menstrual blood.
Sheets.
Soiled, stained.
We are not concerned; the stain is ignored.

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a clear ladder of strictness for stains: regular women, then דיין שעתן women, then a young girl.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus,
as Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said
in the name of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus:
All women: their stains are impure retroactively,
but women about whom the Sages said their time is enough —
their stains are like their sightings,

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִתִּינוֹקֶת שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּהּ לִרְאוֹת,
phrases.english: except for a young girl whose time to see has not arrived,
for even if her sheets are soiled with blood —
we are not concerned for it.
phrases.notes: So for her, the stain makes nothing טמא at all, not even from now on.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס הִיא, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 6 by naming the תנא and quoting his ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The view is רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's, who says that for דיין שעתן women the כתם is like the ראייה.

steps.title: Challenge: Does רבי חנינא even think these women have a stain at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says דיין שעתן women 'have no כתם'. That sounds like their stains cause no טומאה at all, not merely 'like a ראייה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי חנינא hold that there is any stain-impurity at all? But a ברייתא teaches: All women, their stains are impure, and women whose time is enough, their stains are impure. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: Women whose time is enough have no stain-impurity. Doesn't that mean no stain-impurity at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim from Step 7. Another ברייתא makes it look like רבי חנינא holds that these women's stains cause no טומאה whatsoever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7, the stain of a דיין שעתן woman works like her ראייה, so it makes her טמא from now on. In this ברייתא, רבי חנינא says flatly 'they have no כתם,' which suggests zero טומאה. The two quotes seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Does he really hold...?' A challenging question.
At all.
'Isn't it that...?' Suggests a reading of a source in order to attack.
'They have no stain': they have no stain-impurity.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא כֶּתֶם כְּלָל?
phrases.english: And does Rabbi Ḥanina hold of a stain at all?
But isn't it taught: All women, their stains are impure,
and women about whom the Sages said their time is enough —
their stains are impure.
Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says:
women about whom the Sages said their time is enough —
they have no stain.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו אֵין לָהֶן כֶּתֶם כְּלָל?
phrases.english: Isn't it that they have no stain at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא כֶּתֶם כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 7's description of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's view using a different ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס treats the כתם of דיין שעתן women like a ראייה, which is impure from now on.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes him as saying 'אין להן כתם,' which sounds like no stain-impurity at all and so contradicts Step 7.

steps.title: Answer: No stain retroactively, but yes from now on
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'אין להן כתם' means no retroactive stain-impurity. The stain still makes the woman טמא from now on.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means they have no stain-impurity going backward, but they do have stain-impurity from now on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading רבי חנינא's words more narrowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'They have no כתם' only rules out the retroactive part. From the moment it is found, the stain does make the woman טמא, just like a ראייה. That fits exactly with Step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: 'No': rejects the suggested reading.
From now on, going forward.
They do have stain-impurity.

steps.confusionAlert: 'אין להן כתם' does not mean the stain is ignored. It only means the stain doesn't reach back in time.

phrases.english: No, they have no stain retroactively,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יֵשׁ לָהֶן כֶּתֶם מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא.
phrases.english: but they do have a stain from here onward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8 by limiting the meaning of 'אין להן כתם'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אין להן כתם' means no stain-impurity at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means no retroactive stain-impurity; from now on the stain is impure, like a ראייה.

steps.title: So the first opinion makes the stain retroactive even for these women?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי חנינא only denies the retroactive stain, then the first opinion that disagrees with him must hold the stain is retroactive even for דיין שעתן women.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that mean the first תנא holds that it is impure even retroactively?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks what the answer implies about the other opinion in the ברייתא. This sets up the next step, which identifies that opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי חנינא argues only about the retroactive part, the first תנא, who disagrees, must say a כתם is retroactive even for דיין שעתן women. The גמרא asks whether that is really so.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This implies that...': drawing a conclusion from what was just said.
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא.
Even.

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר אֲפִילּוּ לְמַפְרֵעַ?
phrases.english: Does this imply that the first tanna holds even retroactively?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר אֲפִילּוּ לְמַפְרֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks what the answer of Step 9 implies about the first תנא's opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the first תנא really holds that the כתם of a דיין שעתן woman is retroactive.

steps.title: Yes, the first opinion is רבי מאיר, who is strict about stains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees. The first תנא is רבי מאיר, who is strict about כתמים, and a ברייתא shows that he makes the stain retroactive even for דיין שעתן women.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. It is רבי מאיר, who is strict about stains. As a ברייתא teaches: All women, their stains are impure retroactively, and women whose time is enough, their stains are impure retroactively. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא confirms the implication and names the first opinion as רבי מאיר, backing this up with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is known to be strict with כתמים. He treats every woman's stain as retroactive, even a דיין שעתן woman's, although her ראייה is not retroactive. This fully fits the reading of רבי חנינא in Step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes.
Is strict.
Regarding, about.
Blood stains (plural of כֶּתֶם).

steps.whatToRemember: Two views on the stain of a דיין שעתן woman: רבי מאיר says it is retroactive. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says it is טמא only from now on, like a ראייה. רבי חנינא adds that a young girl before the age of seeing has no stain-impurity at all.

phrases.english: Yes, it is Rabbi Meir,
who is stringent about stains.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים — כִּתְמָן טָמֵא לְמַפְרֵעַ,
phrases.english: As it is taught: All women, their stains are impure retroactively,
and women about whom the Sages said their time is enough —
their stains are impure retroactively,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא, דְּמַחְמֵיר גַּבֵּי כְתָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the implication raised in Step 10 and identifies the first תנא as רבי מאיר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The first תנא is רבי מאיר, who makes even a דיין שעתן woman's כתם retroactive.

steps.title: The rest of the ברייתא: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's view
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says the כתם of דיין שעתן women is like their ראייה. A young girl has a כתם only once she has reached the age of seeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: for the women the Sages called 'their time is enough,' their stain is treated like their seeing of blood. A young girl who has reached her time to see blood has stain-impurity. One who has not reached that time has no stain-impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from the last step. This second half shows רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס arguing with רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of this ברייתא already names רבי מאיר outright. So this second half does not prove who the first view belongs to. It shows that רבי חנינא's view, 'their כתם is like their ראייה,' means טמא from now on but not retroactive. That matches the reading in Step 9 and the quote from שמואל in Step 7. He also limits stain-impurity for a young girl to one who has reached the age of seeing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Their time is enough': these women are טמא only from the moment they find blood, not retroactively
A blood stain found on the body or clothing
Actually seeing a flow of blood
A young girl

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says:
Women about whom the Sages said 'their time is enough,'
their stain is like their seeing,
phrases.notes: In other words, the stain makes her טמא only from now on, just like seeing blood does for her.

phrases.english: and a young girl whose time to see has arrived
has a stain,
and one whose time to see has not arrived
has no stain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא brought in step 11, showing the disagreement between רבי חנינא and the first תנא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס holds a דיין שעתן woman's כתם is טמא from now on (like her ראייה) but not retroactively, as Step 9 explained
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second half of רבי מאיר's ברייתא, where רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says 'כתמן כראייתן' and gives the young-girl rule, matching שמואל's quote in Step 7

steps.title: When does a girl reach the age of seeing?
steps.stepSummary: The text asks when a young girl counts as having reached her time to see blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when has she reached her time to see?
steps.whatsHappening: The text asks for a definition of the age mentioned in the last step. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about a young girl's כתם depends on whether she has reached the age of seeing. So that age must be defined.

keyTerms.meaning: She has reached the age when menstrual blood is expected
And when?

phrases.english: And when has her time to see arrived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of a term used in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The age at which a girl is considered to have reached her time to see blood

steps.title: From the days of young womanhood
steps.stepSummary: A girl reaches her time to see once ימי הנעורים have arrived.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when the days of young womanhood have arrived.
steps.whatsHappening: The text answers the question. The age of seeing begins with ימי הנעורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before ימי הנעורים, a stain on a young girl is not assumed to be menstrual blood, so it causes no טומאה. From that point on, her stains count.

keyTerms.meaning: The days of young womanhood, the age of maturity

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס: the כתם of דיין שעתן women is like a ראייה (טמא from now on). A young girl has a כתם only from ימי הנעורים.

phrases.english: From when the days of young womanhood have arrived.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The age of seeing begins at ימי הנעורים

steps.title: A checking cloth used before relations does not count as a full examination
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a woman who has תשמיש using עדים. רב יהודה quotes שמואל: a cloth used before תשמיש does not cut back the retroactive time like a real פקידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And a woman who has relations using checking cloths...' רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: a checking cloth used before relations does not reduce the time the way a real examination does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, about checking cloths during תשמיש. It brings שמואל's rule limiting that line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a פקידה (examination) cuts back how far back the טומאה reaches, because she was found clean at that time. The משנה says checking with עדים during תשמיש works like a פקידה. שמואל says this is not true for a cloth used before תשמיש.

keyTerms.meaning: A checking cloth used to see if blood is present
Marital relations
A deliberate internal examination
Reduces, cuts back the period of retroactive טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not saying the cloth before תשמיש is useless. He is saying it does not shorten the retroactive period the way a full פקידה does.

phrases.english: And a woman who has relations with checking cloths, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which goes on to say that this counts like an examination and shortens the time.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
A cloth used before relations
does not reduce the time like an examination.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, unrelated to the כתם discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cloth used before תשמיש does not shorten the retroactive period like a פקידה

steps.title: Why does the cloth before relations not count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for שמואל's reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a cloth used before תשמיש should be worse than a regular check. This sets up the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A check is a check, so it seems it should work. The גמרא wants to know what makes this one weaker.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind שמואל's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a pre-תשמיש cloth does not count as a פקידה

steps.title: Because she is rushing toward her husband
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא answers that she is in a hurry for her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב קטינא said: because she is hurried and eager for her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: רב קטינא gives the reason: before תשמיש she is rushing and excited for her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her state of mind before תשמיש is different from a calm check. But the answer does not yet explain how that weakens the check, which leads to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Hurried and excited for her husband
Because, since

phrases.english: Rav Ketina said:
Because she is hurried for her household.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב קטינא מתוך שמהומה לביתה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She is rushing toward her husband

steps.title: So what if she is rushing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference her rushing makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if she is hurried for her husband, what of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes for a clearer explanation of how rushing makes the check weaker. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being excited does not by itself change whether blood is present. The גמרא wants the practical link between her rush and the quality of the check.

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? What difference does it make?
And if, so what if

phrases.english: And if she is hurried for her husband,
what of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for further explanation of רב קטינא's reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How her rushing affects the validity of the check

steps.title: She does not check into the folds
steps.stepSummary: Because she is rushing, she does not put the cloth into the recesses and folds, so the check is not thorough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since she is hurried for her husband, she does not insert the cloth into the recesses and folds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the practical point. In her rush she checks only on the surface.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real פקידה requires checking deep into the חורין וסדקין. A shallow check cannot prove she was clean at that moment, so it cannot shorten the retroactive period.

keyTerms.meaning: Recesses and folds, the deep places a proper check must reach
Inserts, puts in

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: a cloth before תשמיש does not count as a פקידה, because in her rush she does not check into the חורין וסדקין.

phrases.english: Since she is hurried for her husband,
she does not insert it into the recesses and folds.

steps.triggerLanguage: מתוך שמהומה לביתה אינה מכנסת לחורין ולסדקין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Her check is not thorough because she does not reach the recesses and folds

steps.title: The משנה says 'cloths', plural: one before and one after?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל. The משנה says 'עדים' (plural), which suggests one cloth before תשמיש and one after, and both count as a פקידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: a woman who has relations with checking cloths, this is like an examination. Isn't it talking about one cloth before relations and one after?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's rule using the wording of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural 'cloths' seems to mean two checks, one before and one after תשמיש. The משנה calls this a פקידה, which would mean a pre-תשמיש cloth does count. That goes against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Checking cloths (plural)
Is it not that...? (a suggested reading used to challenge)

phrases.english: We learned: a woman who has relations with checking cloths,
this is like an examination.
Is it not one before relations
and one after relations?

steps.triggerLanguage: תנן המשמשת בעדים הרי זו כפקידה מאי לאו חד לפני תשמיש וחד לאחר תשמיש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling from step 15 using the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a pre-תשמיש cloth does not count as a פקידה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural 'עדים' suggests one cloth before and one after, and the משנה counts them as a פקידה

steps.title: Both cloths are after relations: one for him, one for her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both cloths are used after תשמיש. One is for the husband and one is for the wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, both are after relations, one for him and one for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by reading the plural differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cloths are not 'before and after' but 'his and hers', both after תשמיש. So the משנה never says a pre-תשמיש cloth counts, and שמואל's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, both
One for him and one for her

phrases.english: No, both this one and that one are after relations,
and one is for him and one is for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the משנה's plural wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'עדים' means one cloth before and one after תשמיש
steps.terutzMaskana: 'עדים' means two cloths after תשמיש, one for him and one for her

steps.title: Support: Jewish women use two cloths, one for him and one for her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its answer with another משנה. Jewish women use two cloths, one for the husband and one for the wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: the custom of Jewish women is to have relations with two checking cloths, one for him and one for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer by showing that 'one for him and one for her' is a known practice from another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the 'his and hers' reading is not made up just to save שמואל. It matches a known custom, so the plural in our משנה fits it naturally.

keyTerms.meaning: The custom of Jewish women

steps.whatToRemember: The plural 'עדים' in the משנה means two cloths after תשמיש, one for him and one for her. So שמואל's rule stands: a cloth before תשמיש is not a פקידה.

phrases.english: As we learned:

phrases.aramaic: דֶּרֶךְ בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל מְשַׁמְּשׁוֹת בִּשְׁנֵי עֵדִים,
phrases.english: The custom of Jewish women is to have relations with two cloths,
one for him and one for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: כדתנן דרך בנות ישראל משמשות בשני עדים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 21 with another משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That 'עדים' refers to two post-תשמיש cloths, one for each spouse
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on 14a about the custom of Jewish women

steps.title: If both cloths are after intercourse, why does the משנה need to say it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 21. If one cloth was before תשמיש, we could understand why the משנה must say it counts. But if both are after תשמיש, it should be obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this? If you say one cloth is before תשמיש and one after, the משנה needed to teach it, because we might think that since she is rushing for her husband she did not check well. So the משנה teaches it still counts as a פקידה. But if you say both are after תשמיש, that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave, that both cloths are used after תשמיש. If that is true, the משנה seems to be telling us something obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A check before תשמיש might be weak because she is rushing, so a משנה saying it counts would teach something new. A check after תשמיש has no rushing problem, so saying it counts seems unnecessary. This means the new reading from step 21 seems to make the משנה's words pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? An opening that points out something does not fit
Granted; this part makes sense
It was needed; the teaching adds something new
You might have thought; the mistaken idea the teaching corrects
It is obvious; why say it at all?
This one and that one; both

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the check before תשמיש is invalid. It is saying that if the משנה were talking about that check, its ruling would teach something new. With two checks after תשמיש, the ruling seems obvious.

phrases.english: What is this?
Granted, if you say
one cloth before intercourse
and one after intercourse,
then it was needed,
because you might have thought:
since she is rushing for her husband
she did not check properly,
so it teaches us
that this counts as a check.
But if you say
that both cloths are after intercourse,
that is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from steps 21-22 that both cloths are after תשמיש
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that both עדים are used after תשמיש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A check after תשמיש has no rushing problem, so a ruling that it counts as a פקידה would be obvious and not worth teaching.

steps.title: A hidden drop of blood under semen is not a worry
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is not obvious. We might have worried that a tiny drop of blood, the size of a mustard seed, was covered by semen and missed. The משנה teaches that we do not worry about this.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: maybe she saw a drop of blood as small as a mustard seed and semen covered it. So the משנה teaches us that it still counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The check after תשמיש has its own possible weakness, so the משנה needed to tell us it still counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After תשמיש, a tiny drop of blood could be hidden under semen, so the check might seem unreliable. The משנה tells us to ignore this worry, and the check counts as a full פקידה. This keeps the reading that both cloths are after תשמיש.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said; it introduces a mistaken idea
A drop of blood the size of a mustard seed
Semen

phrases.english: You might have said,
perhaps she saw a drop of blood like a mustard seed
and semen covered it,
so it teaches us.
phrases.notes: It teaches that we ignore this worry and the check still counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling is not obvious by naming a reasonable worry that the משנה rejects
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A check after תשמיש might not count, because a tiny drop of blood could be hidden under semen.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not worry about hidden blood; the check after תשמיש counts as a פקידה.

steps.title: Second answer: the רבנן required two checks
steps.stepSummary: A different approach: the two cloths are both the wife's. The רבנן required her to check twice, once before and once after תשמיש. The phrase 'it counts as a פקידה' refers only to the check after.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: the רבנן required her to do two checks, one before תשמיש and one after. When the משנה says 'this counts as a פקידה', it means the one after תשמיש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to answer the challenge to שמואל from step 20. This time the plural 'עדים' means two required checks by the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this approach, the plural in the משנה teaches that both checks are required. The 'counts as a פקידה' ruling is attached only to the check after תשמיש. So the check before תשמיש can still be weak because of rushing, as שמואל said, without contradicting the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say; it introduces a second answer
The רבנן required her
Checks, examinations

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
the Rabbis required her two checks,
one before intercourse
and one after intercourse,
and when it teaches 'this counts as a check,'
that refers to the one after intercourse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the challenge against שמואל from step 20, instead of steps 21-24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the plural as two required checks, with the פקידה status given only to the later one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural 'עדים' means both cloths count as a פקידה, including the one before תשמיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both checks are required, but only the one after תשמיש is called a פקידה.

steps.title: The משנה's wording sounds optional
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second answer. The משנה says 'הַמְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת', meaning 'a woman who has relations with cloths'. That sounds like a choice, not a requirement.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה says 'the woman who has relations [with cloths]'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the second answer using the משנה's own wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'הַמְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת' describes what happens if a woman does this, which sounds optional. But the second answer said the רבנן required the checks, so the wording does not seem to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: The woman who has relations; describes a case, which sounds optional
But it teaches...; points to wording that does not fit

phrases.english: But it teaches 'the woman who has relations'!
phrases.notes: This wording sounds like 'if she happens to do it,' not 'she must do it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second answer in step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רבנן required two checks
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording describes an optional case, not a requirement.

steps.title: Read it as 'and she must have relations'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by reading the word differently: 'וּמְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת', meaning 'and she has relations [with cloths]', which works as an instruction.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read the משנה as: 'and she has relations [with cloths].'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording problem by reading the משנה slightly differently, so it tells her what she must do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing 'הַמְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת' to 'וּמְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת' turns a description into an instruction. Now the משנה matches the second answer: she must check before and after תשמיש.

keyTerms.meaning: And she has relations; read as an instruction

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the plural 'עדים': (1) both cloths are after תשמיש, for him and for her, and we ignore a hidden drop under semen; (2) the רבנן required two checks, and only the one after תשמיש is a פקידה, reading 'וּמְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת'.

phrases.english: Read it as: 'and she has relations.'
phrases.notes: The small change makes it an instruction: she is supposed to do this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge in step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: Read 'וּמְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת', meaning the checks are required.

steps.title: Quoting 'it reduces from מעת לעת' and starting a new question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next phrase in the משנה: this check reduces the מעת לעת time. It begins a question: now that it reduces even the מעת לעת...
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says it reduces from מעת לעת. Now that it reduces even from מעת לעת...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next words of the משנה. It begins a question that continues in the next lines, so this step is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says this check shortens both the מעת לעת period and the time back to the last פקידה. The גמרא is starting to ask: if it already shortens the מעת לעת, why does the משנה also need to say it shortens from פקידה to פקידה? The full question continues next.

keyTerms.meaning: Reduces, shortens the time
Here it means 'reduces from'; it shortens
A 24-hour period, during which her purity status is in doubt
Now that; it introduces a 'since this is true...' argument

phrases.english: It reduces from the 24-hour period,
Now that it reduces even from the 24-hour period,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the next phrase of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה needs a second ruling about reducing time, once it already says the check reduces the מעת לעת
